blocks.content: Jharkhand's creation in 2000 was the culmination of a distinct, long-running regional autonomy movement dating back decades before actual statehood — a movement with its own institutional history worth knowing in addition to the final Act of Parliament that created the state.

Demands for a separate state for the Chota Nagpur/Santhal Pargana tribal belt date back to the pre-Independence era, with the Chotanagpur Unnati Samaj (founded 1920) among the earliest organisations articulating tribal political and cultural identity distinct from wider Bihar.

The Jharkhand Party, founded in 1950 by Jaipal Singh Munda (a prominent Adivasi leader, former Constituent Assembly member, and famous as the captain of India's gold-medal-winning 1928 Olympic hockey team), became the primary early political vehicle for the separate-statehood demand, articulating grievances around economic exploitation of the mineral-rich tribal belt by the wider Bihar state administration, cultural/linguistic marginalisation, and the continuing land-alienation concerns rooted in the 19th-century uprisings (Chapter 3).

The movement continued through subsequent decades under various successor organisations, most significantly the Jharkhand Mukti Morcha (JMM), founded in 1972 by Shibu Soren, Binod Bihari Mahato and A.K. Roy, which became the dominant political vehicle for the statehood demand from the 1970s onward and remains one of Jharkhand's principal political parties today (Chapter 5).

★ EXAM POINT: Jaipal Singh Munda — founder of the Jharkhand Party (1950) and a member of India's Constituent Assembly — was ALSO the captain of India's hockey team that won gold at the 1928 Amsterdam Olympics, India's first Olympic hockey gold. This dual sporting-and-political legacy is a frequently tested biographical fact.

After decades of political agitation and several unsuccessful earlier legislative attempts, Parliament passed the Bihar Reorganisation Act, 2000, which formally created the new state of Jharkhand by carving out 18 southern districts from the state of Bihar.

Jharkhand came into existence on 15 November 2000, deliberately timed to coincide with Birsa Munda's birth anniversary (Chapter 3) — making Jharkhand, along with Chhattisgarh (carved from Madhya Pradesh) and Uttarakhand (carved from Uttar Pradesh), one of three new states created in the same year, 2000, as part of a broader wave of state reorganisation driven by similar regional-identity and development-grievance movements.

Babulal Marandi (BJP) became Jharkhand's first Chief Minister, and Ranchi was designated the state capital (also serving as the historic administrative centre of the Chota Nagpur division under British rule).
